currency_assumptions: Venue prices are stored in HKD (cost_local_amount / cost_local_currency = HKD). Every USD figure uses the ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates dated 2026-11-27 and fetched 2026-11-28: EUR 1 = USD 1.0957 and EUR 1 = HKD 8.5774, giving USD 1 = HKD 7.828238 and 1 HKD = USD 0.12774267. See fx_evidence_2026-11-28.md for the worked cross rate and three hand recomputations.

Where a venue publishes an hourly rate, the recorded amount is that rate x 8 hours (the acceptable 09:00-17:00 window), stated in evidence.observed_facts. Where a venue publishes a day or session package, the recorded amount is that package and cost_rate_unit says which: 'day' for Igather Central's HK$10,000 full day, 'event' for the Sheung Wan Civic Centre lecture hall's HK$1,330 four-hour session. Packages therefore differ in length, so the USD figures are prices for each venue's own published package, not hour-for-hour comparisons.

Two venues publish a bare '$' with no currency marker. Dream Impact's Chinese-language Hong Kong page is read as HKD (its rates are plausible Hong Kong rates) and carries a confirm-currency question. Good Lab's page prints a bare '$' while its embedded Webflow currency setting declares USD, so its cost is left null with a confirm-currency question rather than converted.

Venues that publish no price at all (AMO, The Hive Kennedy Town, The Hive Wan Chai, Banyan Workspace, The Wave, Good Lab, PMQ, Hong Kong Science Park) carry estimated_cost_usd null with a cost_unknown question. Null is not free and is not a rejection.
No date is selected, ranked or recommended in this run. The whole 2027 calendar year was swept; the venue set is date-independent and every venue carries its own Saturday-availability question.

Alcohol is treated as a licensing question everywhere. No venue's page in this sweep states that an event alcohol licence or permission is in place, so every record carries a booking_terms question about serving alcohol and any licence requirement; no hotel bar is read as a yes.

declared_gaps.text: The HK rows of pinned registry edition 3b20667d are seventeen gazetted 2027 general holidays plus one public-holiday coverage row; they carry no school_holiday row. Re-checked 2026-11-28, the Education Bureau school-calendar index publishes only 2026/27 documents and no 2027/28 example calendar, and the EDB legacy school-calendar paths return HTTP 404 (captures/coverage_school_hk_edb_index.html, captures/coverage_school_hk_edb_legacy_404.html). The store therefore asserts no Hong Kong school date for the 2027/28 school year (2027-09-01 to 2028-08-31); it does not say the 2026/27 school year has no holidays, which this check did not establish.

Eight of the sixteen venues publish no event-space rate at all — AMO, The Hive Kennedy Town, The Hive Wan Chai, Banyan Workspace, The Wave, Good Lab, PMQ and Hong Kong Science Park — so their cost is unknown rather than zero. Dream Impact's bare "$" is read as HKD under a stated currency assumption, and Good Lab's bare "$" is left unconverted because its own page declares USD. The priced rates are not one product: six are an hourly rate x 8 hours (one of them, Ngau Chi Wan, derived from the published hourly rate), Igather Central is a full-day package, and the Sheung Wan Civic Centre lecture hall is a four-hour session. On the page the five hourly-rate rooms without a recorded `estimated_hours` print their USD figure beside an "unknown 8h" window label; the amount is the recorded rate x 8 hours, but the record itself does not state the hours its figure covers.
Each of the sixteen room records rests on a single operator or LCSD page for its capacity, rate, hours and equipment; no second independent source was found for any room, and the record dates say so.

Four of the sixteen venues carry no room photograph and store an explicit withheld record instead: Igather Kwun Tong (no image tied to the 20-40-person room), The Hive Wan Chai (only a location-card image, no caption for the 21/F space), PMQ QUBE (one 5,760 x 3,840 / 9.4 MB original with no smaller variant) and Hong Kong Science Park (no image of the Charles K. Kao Auditorium on the captured page). Dream Impact's single image shows Synergy A/B, one of the four booked rooms, not the combined whole. No Wikimedia image was used: no Commons file on a captured page depicts one of these hired rooms.

The three local-requirement claims record the city-level rules for language, alcohol and food. They do not say which licence a given venue holds or whether a 50-person private event is covered by it: alcohol and catering stay booking-terms questions on every room, and the food claim records the licence types and the caterer route without deciding the event's own position.

Fourteen of the sixteen rooms publish no booking window at all, so the 12-hour preferred programme is confirmed nowhere. Two records (Igather Central, AMO) publish an all-day opening statement that the approved research bundle scored `allows_to_6`, and no room publishes a covered 09:00-21:00 hire interval; a 09:00 start with an 8-hour floor is the only window the evidence supports.

Eight 2027 calendar rows, each organiser-dated and captured: Consensus Hong Kong 2027 (2027-02-02..03), Hong Kong Web3 Festival 2027 (2027-04-19..21), AIAIS 2027 (2027-01-22..24), AI 2030 Summit Hong Kong 2027 (2027-01-25), the Standard Chartered Hong Kong Marathon 2027 (2027-01-17), Art Basel Hong Kong 2027 (2027-03-25..27), Art Central 2027 (2027-03-24..28) and the Cathay/HSBC Hong Kong Sevens 2027 (2027-04-09..11). No date is recommended and none of the eight is booked.

Two mandatory discovery lanes could not be read from Hong Kong: Peerspace returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge and Venue Report returned HTTP 403 and lands on its home page with no Hong Kong coverage; Tagvenue and Eventective have no Hong Kong inventory. The five programme-wide mandatory sources (Miragather x3, AI Tinkerers, the DeAI Luma feed) carry no check date in this store because the Hong Kong research bundle did not record them, and the page prints that fact.

All sixteen records are building, street or area tier from the saved Nominatim response; no room entrance was verified. Seven are building-tier, seven street-tier and two area-tier: The Hive Kennedy Town sits on a playground node on Smithfield Road rather than the building at 12P Smithfield Road, and Hong Kong Science Park is a whole-site point.

evidence.observed_facts: Section 166 names Good Friday as a general holiday and the federal labour standards page (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/jobs/workplace/federal-labour-standards/vacations-holidays.html) lists it among the ten. Good Friday is the Friday before Easter Sunday: the Ontario Ministry of Education 2026-27 school year calendar states 'Friday, March 26 is Easter Friday and Monday, March 29 is Easter Monday' and the Government of British Columbia 2027 statutory-holiday table lists 'Good Friday | Friday, March 26', which fixes 26 March 2027.

evidence.observed_facts: Schulzeitgesetz 1985 § 2 Abs 4 Z 3 makes 24 December to 6 January the statutory Christmas school-free period in every year; in 2027/28 that is Friday 24 December 2027 to Thursday 6 January 2028. The optional 23 December extension applies only when 23 December is a Monday (it is a Thursday in 2027), and no ordinance declaring 23 December 2027 or 7 January 2028 free is published, so the statutory span is recorded. The Vienna 2027/28 school-year edition is not published, so this row rests on the statute alone.

holidays.source_edition: Schulzeitgesetz 1985 § 2 Abs 4 Z 3, RIS-Fassung vom 21.10.2026
holidays.source_locator: § 2 Abs 4 Z 3: 'die Tage vom 24. Dezember bis einschließlich 6. Jänner (Weihnachtsferien); der 23. Dezember, sofern er auf einen Montag fällt; überdies können der 23. Dezember sowie der 7. Jänner, wenn es für einzelne Schulen aus Gründen der Ab- oder Anreise der Schüler zweckmäßig ist, von der zuständigen Schulbehörde durch Verordnung schulfrei erklärt werden'
holidays.source_title: Schulzeitgesetz 1985 - Bundesrecht konsolidiert, Fassung vom 21.10.2026

evidence.observed_facts: Schulzeitgesetz 1985 § 2 Abs 4 Z 2 declares 'der Allerseelentag' school-free, and the BMB page lists 'der Allerseelentag (2. November)' under 'Schulfrei sind - abgesehen von den Sonntagen -'. The date is fixed at 2 November in every year, so the 2027 occurrence is Tuesday 2 November 2027. Allerseelen is not one of Austria's statutory public holidays (the AT public layer carries the thirteen gesetzliche Feiertage and none falls on 2 November), so the day is recorded here as a school_holiday row. The Vienna directorate 2026/2027 page lists the same date in its 'Schulfreie Tage' section for 2026 ('Allerheiligen, Allerseelen: Sonntag, 1. November und Montag, 2. November 2026'), confirming that Vienna observes it. Direct access to ris.bka.gv.at from the curation host answers HTTP 503, so the wording was read through the search backend's fetch of the consolidated page https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/GeltendeFassung.wxe?Abfrage=Bundesnormen&Gesetzesnummer=10009575. That page's 'Fassung vom' header label was not stable across fetches on 2026-11-20 (21.10.2026, 18.11.2026 and 19.11.2026 were each printed by a fetch of the same URL), so this row cites the statute by Gesetzesnummer and asserts no Fassung date.

The row keeps the stated full bounds although it starts before the 2027-01-01 window start. Vyhláška 16/2005 Sb. § 4 odst. 3 fixes the break as 23 December to 2 January inclusive with an end extension only when 3 January is a Friday; in 2026/27 2 January is a Saturday, so the ministry's stated Sunday end adds only the weekend day on which no teaching takes place.

alcohol.quote: It is an offence under Section 17(3B) of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109) to sell liquor without a licence. A person convicted of the offence is liable to a fine of $1,000,000 and imprisonment for 2 years. In this connection, any person who intends to sell liquor at any premises for consumption on those premises must obtain a liquor licence issued by the Liquor Licensing Board before commencement of such business. … In general, the Liquor Licensing Board considers applications for liquor licences if the premises to which the applications relate are licensed general/light refreshment/marine restaurants (full or provisional), or likely to be licensed or provisionally licensed by the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene. A liquor licence will be issued when the premises have been issued with a restaurant licence or a provisional restaurant licence. … The Liquor Licensing Board will also consider applications for liquor licence in respect of premises other than the afore-mentioned. For such premises not under application for or not covered by a valid restaurant licence or Certificate of Compliance … the processing time of such liquor licence applications will be longer.
alcohol.source_locator: captures/claim_alcohol_hk_llb_note.html — "Important Notes", first bullet (line 37), last revised 2018-09-20; captures/claim_alcohol_hk_llb_policy.html — "Policy / New Issue", the restaurant-licence paragraph and the "other premises" paragraph (line 43), last revised 2026-11-04. Both pages are published by the Liquor Licensing Board (酒牌局).
alcohol.source_title: Liquor Licensing Board (酒牌局) — Important Notes and Policy

value.authority: Liquor Licensing Board (酒牌局), the statutory body under the Dutiable Commodities (Liquor) Regulations (Cap. 109 sub. leg. B); FEHD provides its executive and secretarial support
value.licence_required_for: any person who intends to sell liquor at any premises for consumption on those premises, before the business begins
value.not_established: these pages do not say whether serving liquor without selling it (a free bar) needs a licence, which party — venue, caterer or organiser — must hold the licence for a 50-person private event, or whether any room in this sweep would be approved. Alcohol therefore stays a booking-terms question on every venue and no hotel bar is read as a yes
value.offence: selling liquor without a licence is an offence under s.17(3B) of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109); on conviction a fine of $1,000,000 (HKD) and imprisonment for 2 years
value.premises_route: in general the Board considers premises licensed as general, light refreshment or marine restaurants (full or provisional) and issues the liquor licence once the restaurant licence is issued; it will also consider other premises, with more departments consulted and a longer processing time

food.quote: A restaurant licence must be obtained from the DFEH for the food business which involves the sale of meals or unbottled non-alcoholic drinks other than Chinese herb tea, for consumption on the premises, but does not include a factory canteen or any business carried on by a hawker … A food factory licence must be obtained from DFEH for the food business which involves the preparation of food for sale for human consumption off the premises … operating a take-away food shop or providing catering service, etc. … A temporary food factory licence must be obtained from DFEH for the food business which involves the operation of a stall/kiosk of temporary nature for sale of heating up / warming pre-cooked food and/or cooking of pre-prepared, ready-to-cook food for human consumption off the premises in conjunction with a public function (e.g. exhibitions, shows, sports competitions, concerts, etc.) of short duration before commencement of such business. The validity period of a temporary food factory licence will not exceed 7 days.
food.source_locator: captures/claim_food_hk_fehd_types.html — "Restaurant Licence" (line 48), "Food Factory Licence" (line 60) with list item "operating a take-away food shop or providing catering service, etc." (line 65), and "Temporary Food Factory Licence" (line 78); the captured page is last revised 2026-09-29
food.source_title: FEHD (食物環境衞生署) — Guide on Types of Licences Required

value.authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (食物環境衞生署, FEHD)
value.event_implication: a caterer supplying the event is expected to hold a food factory licence as a "catering service", and a venue selling meals on its premises needs a restaurant licence
value.food_factory_licence: required for a food business that prepares food for sale for consumption off the premises; "operating a take-away food shop or providing catering service" is listed among the trades it covers
value.not_established: the page does not say which licence a 50-person private event in a hired room operates under, whether food given away free counts as a sale, or which licence any venue in this sweep holds — catering stays a booking-terms question on every venue
value.restaurant_licence: required for a food business that sells meals or unbottled non-alcoholic drinks for consumption on the premises
value.temporary_food_factory_licence: required for a temporary stall or kiosk selling heated pre-cooked food or pre-prepared ready-to-cook food in conjunction with a public function such as an exhibition, show, sports competition or concert; valid for no more than 7 days

language.quote: Chinese and English are the official languages of Hong Kong. English is widely used in the Government and by the legal, professional and business sectors.
